claim: spec/merkle/arch_snapshot_store.md, "Read vs. write call sites", states twice that Save has no production caller: "Save therefore has no production caller", and "There is no other writer — no standalone `spex hash` command, no other subcommand that persists the tree." The same section's Load discussion also asserts the seed snapshot `spex init` writes is produced "in exactly one place" without naming what writes it. merkle/snapshot_store.go:58's doc comment on Save ("it has no production caller") repeats the same claim.
authoritative_source: spec/lifecycle/arch_init_command.md, "Behaviour": "spex init writes exactly two files into a fresh .spex/" including "The snapshot, seeded with the canonical empty tree," which requires init to persist a snapshot to disk as part of its normal, successful run — a production code path, not a test.
evidence: InitCommand (this bead) must call some snapshot-persisting function on its happy path. The only function SnapshotStore exposes for writing a tree straight to a path is Save (Encode returns bytes only; the temp-file-and-rename write ingest uses is unexported inside the ingest package and not reachable from cmd/spex without a layering violation). Calling merkle.Save from cmd/spex/init.go, as this PR does, makes Save a production caller for the first time, which directly falsifies arch_snapshot_store.md's "Save therefore has no production caller" and "no other subcommand that persists the tree," and falsifies the doc comment at merkle/snapshot_store.go:58 that repeats the same claim. The two leaves do not name a resolution — arch_snapshot_store.md was written before InitCommand existed and does not carve out an exception for it, and arch_init_command.md does not say which SnapshotStore function init should call. Deciding whether init keeps calling Save (and the call-site inventory in arch_snapshot_store.md is updated to name it) or init gets its own atomic seed-write helper (leaving Save's "no production caller" claim true) is an authoring-loop call, not an implementer's.
proposed_fix: In the authoring loop, either (a) update spec/merkle/arch_snapshot_store.md's "Read vs. write call sites" to add `spex init` as Save's one production caller, and correct the doc comment at merkle/snapshot_store.go:58 accordingly, since init's seed write does not need atomicity (it only ever writes into a directory it just created and refuses to run at all if `.spex/` already exists, so there is no live file for a reader to observe mid-write); or (b) give InitCommand its own minimal seed-write helper that does not route through Save, preserving "Save has no production caller" as stated. This PR keeps calling merkle.Save (option (a)'s code shape) pending that decision, since it is the only presently-available way to persist the seed snapshot without reaching into ingest's unexported write path.
